shared.jobCompose.noTitle: Give the job a title. It is what the list shows later.
shared.jobCompose.titleTooLong: The title is too long to read in a list. Keep it under 120 characters.
shared.jobCompose.noSteps: Add at least one command. Blank lines and # comments do not count.
shared.jobCompose.tooManySteps: {{steps}} steps is more than the {{max}} this dialog can show you at once, and a confirmation nobody can read is not one.
shared.jobCompose.tooManyRollbackSteps: The rollback has more than {{max}} steps, which is more than the dialog can show you.
shared.jobCompose.badWaveSize: The wave size must be a whole number, or 0 for all servers at once.
shared.jobCompose.waveTooBig: A wave of {{size}} servers is more than this will run at once. Use {{max}} or fewer.
shared.jobCompose.gateNeedsWaves: The health gate holds each wave until the previous one is healthy, so it needs more than one wave. Set a wave size smaller than the number of servers, or untick the gate.
shared.envWrite.disclosure: OpsMaxx has never read this file’s values and does not read them to make this change: it writes the value you pick from the vault over the line with this name, or adds the line if there is none. It cannot tell you whether the value is already the same one.
shared.maintenance.noServers: Choose the servers this window covers. A window over nothing silences nothing.
shared.maintenance.inThePast: That time has already passed, so the window would end before it began.
shared.maintenance.tooLong: A window can run for at most {{max}} hours. A longer silence is one nobody remembers setting — open another when this one ends.
shared.maintenance.noNote: Say what the window is for. Somebody reading the alert log in three weeks will want to know why it went quiet.
shared.maintenance.describe: {{count}} server(s) — {{names}} — stop announcing alerts for {{hours}}h. They keep being sampled and their chips stay up; what stops is the notifications. Webhook endpoints still receive everything.
shared.terminalTheme.notJson: That file is not valid JSON.
shared.terminalTheme.noCompleteScheme: No scheme in that file has all sixteen colours.
shared.terminalTheme.noScheme: That file contains no colour scheme.
shared.terminalTheme.badColour: "{{key}}" is missing or is not a #rrggbb colour.
shared.terminalTheme.notIterm: That file is not an iTerm2 colour preset.
shared.terminalTheme.unrecognised: Unrecognised file. Import an iTerm2 .itermcolors or a Windows Terminal scheme.
shared.userStep.badUser: A user name may only be lower-case letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, and may not start with a digit or hyphen. This text runs as root.
shared.userStep.protectedUser: OpsMaxx will not change {{user}}. Locking or deleting it can take away the only way back into a server, and no confirmation makes that recoverable from here.
shared.userStep.badGroup: Name the group, in the same character set as a user name.
shared.userStep.badExpiry: The expiry date must be YYYY-MM-DD, or empty to remove the expiry.
shared.engineUpgrade.liveRestoreOn: This daemon reports live-restore ON, so containers are configured to keep running across a daemon restart. That is what the daemon says about itself; nothing here has watched it happen.
shared.engineUpgrade.liveRestoreOff: This daemon reports live-restore OFF: restarting it stops every container on this server, and the upgrade restarts it.
shared.engineUpgrade.liveRestoreOffCount: This daemon reports live-restore OFF: restarting it stops all {{count}} running container(s) on this server, and the upgrade restarts it.
shared.engineUpgrade.liveRestoreUnknown: The daemon did not say whether live-restore is on, so whether this stops every container on the server is unknown rather than no.
shared.engineUpgrade.allPackages: All four of Docker’s packages are upgraded together. Upgrading only the daemon leaves a CLI and a container runtime from the previous release beside it.
shared.engineUpgrade.configuredRepo: This upgrades from whichever repository the server is configured with. It does not add one, and it does not pin a version.
shared.sudoers.gap.truncated: the file was longer than this reads
shared.sudoers.claimWithGaps: {{claim}} — but {{gaps}}, so this is not the whole picture.
shared.sudoers.none: No sudoers rule names this account
shared.sudoers.anyNoPassword: Can run ANY command, WITHOUT a password
shared.sudoers.anyWithPassword: Can run any command, with a password
shared.sudoers.listedNoPassword: Can run {{count}} listed command set(s) without a password
shared.sudoers.namedSomeNoPassword: Named by {{count}} rule(s), some of whose commands need no password
shared.sudoers.namedWithPassword: Named by {{count}} rule(s), with a password
shared.sudoers.filesUnreadable: {{base}} — and {{count}} file(s) could not be read ({{files}}), which usually means this sweep was not root.
shared.graphql.variablesNotObject: Variables must be a JSON object, like { "id": 1 }.
shared.graphql.notJson: The endpoint answered with something that is not JSON. It may not be a GraphQL endpoint.
shared.graphql.notJsonStatus: The endpoint answered {{status}} with something that is not JSON.
shared.graphql.notObject: A GraphQL response is a JSON object.
shared.openapiImport.tooLarge: That description is larger than 32 MB.
shared.openapiImport.unreadable: Could not read it as JSON or YAML: {{error}}
shared.openapiImport.notOpenApi: That is not an OpenAPI description.
shared.openapiImport.upgradeFailed: Could not upgrade the Swagger 2 description: {{error}}
shared.openapiImport.unsupportedVersion: That is not an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 description.
shared.apiOpenApi.badPathItem: The path item is an external reference, or not an object.
shared.apiOpenApi.badOperation: The operation is not an object.
shared.httpClient.privateKeyInCa: That file contains a private key. Only the CA certificate is needed; choose a file with just the certificate.
shared.httpClient.noCertificate: No PEM certificate (-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----) was found in that file.
shared.credentialShape.none: OpsMaxx has no credential saved for this connection, so it offered none. Add a key, a password or an agent in Edit connection. If it is saved on another of your devices, move it into the vault there (Vault, Move into the vault) and this device can use it.
shared.credentialShape.vaultLocked: This connection authenticates from the vault, and the vault is locked, so nothing could be offered. Unlock it and try again.
shared.credentialShape.key: OpsMaxx offered the private key at {{path}}. If that key is not in this account's authorized_keys, the server refuses it whatever the username.
shared.credentialShape.agent: OpsMaxx offered whatever keys your SSH agent holds. If the agent has none loaded, the server sees no credential at all — check with ssh-add -l.
shared.enginePrecheck.refusal.noRepo: Docker publishes no repository for this package manager, so there are no docker-ce packages to upgrade. Whatever engine this server runs came from somewhere else, and upgrading it is that source’s business.
shared.enginePrecheck.refusal.notInstall: Read what the precheck listed and confirm docker-ce is actually installed. If this server runs an engine from somewhere else — Debian’s docker.io, or a distribution package — installing docker-ce would put a SECOND, conflicting engine on the machine rather than upgrading the one that is there, and nothing in this build can tell those two cases apart from the package manager’s output.
shared.enginePrecheck.refusal.unchecked: Nothing has been read from this server yet. Run the precheck first: what is installed and whether the daemon keeps containers running across a restart are both facts about this host, and neither can be assumed.
shared.topology.hopViaMissing: {{hop}} (saved server {{via}}, which is not in this list)
shared.topology.unmatchedHops_one: {{count}} hop is not backed by a saved server (on {{who}}), so the reboot checks below cannot see them. Two servers can share a bastion that OpsMaxx has never been told about; if one of the servers below is that machine, nothing here will say so.
shared.topology.unmatchedHops_other: {{count}} hops are not backed by a saved server (on {{who}}), so the reboot checks below cannot see them. Two servers can share a bastion that OpsMaxx has never been told about; if one of the servers below is that machine, nothing here will say so.
shared.topology.byAddress_one: {{names}} names that hop by the address {{addresses}} rather than by a saved-server reference; {{name}} is the saved server at that address. The same machine reached under two names is exactly the case a serverId-only check cannot see, so it is refused here rather than counted as an unmatched hop. If they are genuinely different machines, correct the server or port on one of them.
shared.topology.byAddress_other: {{names}} name that hop by the address {{addresses}} rather than by a saved-server reference; {{name}} is the saved server at that address. The same machine reached under two names is exactly the case a serverId-only check cannot see, so it is refused here rather than counted as an unmatched hop. If they are genuinely different machines, correct the server or port on one of them.
shared.topology.jumpHost_one: {{name}} is the jump host that {{via}} connects through. Restarting it drops those connections — including the ones this job is using to watch its own work — so this run will not do it. Reboot it on its own, deliberately, with nothing else in flight.
shared.topology.jumpHost_other: {{name}} is the jump host that {{via}} connect through. Restarting it drops those connections — including the ones this job is using to watch its own work — so this run will not do it. Reboot it on its own, deliberately, with nothing else in flight.
shared.topology.sameWaveDatabase: {{names}} both carry a saved {{db}} database, and this wave would restart them together. OpsMaxx does not know whether they replicate — it only knows you saved the same database on both — so it will not restart them in the same wave. Put them in different waves.
